_provenance_note: Multi-country building-fire F-N curve dataset compiled 2026-08-27. Each curve's F(>=N) values are cumulative exceedance frequencies (events per year with >= N deaths). Population is mid-period national estimate. All values derived from primary sources cited per curve. NEVER add a curve without source, pop_millions, and a primary-source read.
figure_note: Scopes differ by source and are stated per curve. For cross-country comparison, normalise F by pop_millions to get events per million population per year.

curves.label: Singapore 2012-2025, building envelope (this study)
curves.source: Event-resolved register compiled from SCDF annual releases and coroner reports. Manuscript Section 4. 47 events, 64 deaths, max N=4.

curves.label: China 1998-2002, all fires (Wang et al. 2005)
curves.source: Wang F, Lu S, Li C. Fire Safety Science 8:353-362 (2005), DOI 10.3801/iafss.fss.8-353. Cumulative F(>=N) derived from per-year incident counts in Table 4 (p.359). Population 1,266 million (year 2000) as stated in Table 1.

curves.label: England 2010/11-2018/19, building fires (Home Office)
curves.scope: building fires only (Shoreham N=11 outdoor aircraft crash excluded); England, not UK
curves.source: An in-depth review of fire-related fatalities and severe casualties in England, 2010/11 to 2018/19. UK Home Office/MHCLG (2019), Table 2. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/an-in-depth-review-of-fire-related-fatalities-and-severe-casualties-in-england-2010-to-201819. N=71 is Grenfell Tower (14 Jun 2017; IRS toll 71, official final toll 72). Population: ONS mid-year estimates, average 2010-2018 = 54.4M.
curves.notes: No data points between N=7 and N=70 (no building fire killed 7-70 people in this window). This gap is genuine data, not missing data.

curves.label: USA 2018-2023, residential building fires (USFA)
curves.scope: residential building fires only; non-residential structure fires excluded (~25% of all fire deaths)
curves.source: USFA TFRS v22i2 (2018-2020 fatal fires, 87%/10%/3% distribution) + USFA TFRS v23i1 (2021-2023 multi-fatality breakdown: 76.8%/14.3%/4.7%/4.2%). 1,900 fatal fires/year from national estimates. N>=5 bucket is aggregated (4.2% of multi-fatality fires). Population: US Census ~332M. Primary URLs: https://www.usfa.fema.gov/downloads/pdf/statistics/v22i2.pdf, https://www.usfa.fema.gov/statistics/reports/who-fire-impacts/multiple-fatality-fires-in-residential-buildings-v23i1.html
curves.notes: F values are already annualised (T=1). The 5+ tail is aggregated; NFPA Catastrophic Multiple-Death Fires report has detail but is paywalled. Distribution derived from two overlapping periods; proportion-based, not raw counts for a single period.

curves.label: Sweden 1999-2013, residential fires (Jonsson et al.)
curves.scope: residential fires only; ~5/6 of all Swedish fatal fires
curves.source: Jonsson et al. The state of the residential fire fatality problem in Sweden. J Safety Res 2017;63:183-191. Sardqvist & Holmstedt, Characteristics of fatal residential fires in Sweden (Brandforsk report). 1,183 incidents / 1,292 deaths. Per-incident distribution reconstructed from aggregate constraint (109 extra deaths) and 1988-2000 proportional data (~92% single, ~6% double, ~1% triple, ~1% quad+). Population: SCB mid-period ~9.5M.
curves.notes: RECONSTRUCTED per-incident distribution. Exact counts require the Brandforsk PDF (confirmed at brandskyddsforeningen.se) or MSB IDA database (ida.msb.se). The aggregate constraint (1183 incidents, 1292 deaths) is firm; the per-N split carries uncertainty of roughly +-15% at N>=2. Gothenburg discotheque fire (1998, 63 deaths) is outside this window and non-residential.

curves.label: Australia FY2004-2017, preventable residential fires (Coates et al. 2019)
curves.scope: preventable residential fires only; final 2-3 years under-reported 7-23% per source
curves.source: Coates L et al. Preventable Residential Fire Fatalities in Australia July 2003 to June 2017. BNHCRC Report 506.2019, Table 8 p.40. Population: ABS mid-window mean 22,185,900.

curves.label: New Zealand 2007-2014, unintentional domestic fires (Lilley & McNoe 2018)
curves.source: Lilley R, McNoe B. Unintentional Domestic Fire-Related Fatal Injury in New Zealand: 2007-2014. FENZ Research Report 167 (2018). Population: Stats NZ mid-window mean 4,367,350.
